title: Conjecture 1.2
statement_text: Let $G$ be a strongly 2-connected digraph drawn (possibly with crossings) in an annulus $\Sigma$, such that every directed cycle has winding number one around the annulus in the natural sense. Then $G$ can be drawn in $\Sigma$ without crossings, such that every directed cycle has winding number one.
context_text: In this paper a digraph has no loops or parallel edges, but directed cycles of length two are allowed. A digraph is strongly 2-connected if (in the usual sense; the paper does not define it) it has at least three vertices and remains strongly connected after deleting any one vertex. A digraph $G$ is weightable if one can assign a real weight $w(e)$ to each edge $e$ such that $\sum_{e\in E(C)}w(e)=1$ for every directed cycle $C$. Drawing in an annulus is the same as drawing in the plane avoiding the origin; in such a drawing each edge subtends a fraction $w(e)$ of a full turn around the origin, so $G$ is weightable if and only if it can be drawn (possibly with crossings) in an annulus so that every directed cycle has winding number one. The conjecture arises from a theorem of Thomassen: if $G$ is acyclic with sources $a,b$ and sinks $c,d$ (all distinct) and every other vertex has in- and out-degree at least two, then exactly one holds: there are vertex-disjoint directed paths from $a$ to $c$ and from $b$ to $d$, or $G$ can be drawn in a closed disc with $a,b,c,d$ in order on the boundary. Viewing this as a drawing in a rectangle with sources on the north side and sinks on the south side, and gluing north to south (identifying $a=d$, $b=c$), gives an annulus in which crossings can be removed iff every directed cycle winds exactly once; the conjecture asks whether this extends to strongly 2-connected digraphs. The author states that this would be a pretty extension of Thomassen's theorem but that he cannot prove it. Checking the case where all weights are equal ($\ell$-cyclic digraphs, in which every directed cycle has length $\ell$) gives no evidence, since no $\ell$-cyclic digraph is strongly 2-connected; the paper instead gives a construction of all 3-cyclic digraphs.
paper_title: When all directed cycles have length three

title: Informal Question (NP-characterization of weightable digraphs)
statement_text: Can we give a construction for all weightable digraphs (i.e., an NP-characterization)?
context_text: In this paper a digraph has no loops or parallel edges, but directed cycles of length two are allowed. A digraph is strongly 2-connected if (in the usual sense; the paper does not define it) it has at least three vertices and remains strongly connected after deleting any one vertex. A digraph $G$ is weightable if one can assign a real weight $w(e)$ to each edge $e$ such that $\sum_{e\in E(C)}w(e)=1$ for every directed cycle $C$. Drawing in an annulus is the same as drawing in the plane avoiding the origin; in such a drawing each edge subtends a fraction $w(e)$ of a full turn around the origin, so $G$ is weightable if and only if it can be drawn (possibly with crossings) in an annulus so that every directed cycle has winding number one. The author shows that $G$ is weightable if and only if no subdigraph of $G$ is a weak $k$-double cycle with $k\ge3$ (a notion from the theory of even directed cycles), by the same proof as for even digraphs but over the reals instead of $GF(2)$; this excluded-subdigraph characterization is a co-NP characterization. He also shows that every weightable digraph has a $\{0,1\}$-valued weighting. An NP-characterization would be an explicit construction producing exactly the weightable digraphs. For strongly 2-connected digraphs, the author's conjecture that any such digraph drawable in an annulus with all directed cycles of winding number one can be redrawn there without crossings would give such a construction, but it remains open; the paper gives a construction for the special case of 3-cyclic digraphs (all directed cycles of length three), and the case of 4-cyclic digraphs is open.
notes: Stated as prose question in the introduction without a labelled environment.
paper_title: When all directed cycles have length three
